title: Fake Job Offer Scams — Warning Signs and Protection
publisher: Cyber Dost, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
text: Fake job offer scams are widespread in India, particularly targeting students and first-time job seekers. These scams promise high-paying work-from-home jobs, data entry roles, or part-time tasks with unrealistic salaries (Rs 30,000–50,000/month with no experience required). Warning signs: (1) Registration fee — Any job that asks you to pay a fee to 'register', 'get materials', 'buy a kit', or 'secure your slot' is a scam. Legitimate employers never charge candidates. (2) No interview — Instant job offers without any interview, resume review, or verification process. (3) Advance payment — Asking you to pay first to 'unlock' tasks or earnings. (4) Payment to claim payment — 'Your first payment is Rs 5,000 — just pay Rs 500 GST/tax to release it.' This is always a scam. (5) Vague company details — no verifiable address, no company registration number, no LinkedIn presence. What to do: Never pay any amount for a job. Verify the company on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs portal (mca.gov.in). Report fake job ads at cybercrime.gov.in. Legitimate job portals: Naukri, LinkedIn, Internshala — these never charge job seekers.
